channel.title: Xsatori Labs — Insights
channel.description: How we scope, price, and ship software — from the team behind Hookah Royale, Flat OS, Xsatori, NMWWD, and Credit4Vets.

item.title: Building software on a nonprofit budget
item.description: Nonprofits get quoted like enterprises and funded like side projects. Here's how we scope technology work when every dollar is donated.

item.title: What an MVP actually is (and what twelve weeks really buys you)
item.description: "Minimum viable product" has been stretched to mean anything. Here's the definition that's actually useful when you're paying for the build.

item.title: Seven signs your business has outgrown its spreadsheets
item.description: Spreadsheets scale further than people expect and then fail suddenly. Here's how to recognize the transition before it costs you a customer.

item.title: Fixed bid vs. time and materials: which contract actually protects you
item.description: Fixed bid feels safer and often isn't. Here's what each structure really does to incentives, and how to pick without getting burned.

item.title: Building Hookah Royale: real-time multiplayer on a small team
item.description: A case study in shipping synchronized card games across web, iOS, and Android — and the architectural decisions that kept the team small.

item.title: Build vs. buy: when internal software is worth writing yourself
item.description: Most companies should buy. Here's the specific set of conditions under which building your own internal system actually pays back, and how to tell which side you're on.

item.title: The cold-start problem: why marketplaces fail before they launch
item.description: Most failed marketplaces had working software. What they didn't have was a credible plan for the first ninety days of emptiness.

item.title: What a two-sided marketplace actually costs to build
item.description: Most marketplace quotes are wrong because they price the wrong thing. Here's where the money actually goes, and which line items nobody warns you about.
